text:
Me: "Two ribeyes, please. Just the steaks."
Waiter: "Two ribeyes for the table?"
Me: "Two ribeyes for me."
Waiter: [does not write this down]
Me: "Both medium rare."
Waiter: "Are you waiting for someone?"
Me: "No."
Waiter: "Right."
He leaves. He returns with a more senior waiter.
Senior Waiter: "Sir, I understand you'd like two ribeyes."
Me: "Yes."
Senior Waiter: "Together?"
Me: "One after the other is fine."
Senior Waiter: "And no sides."
Me: "Correct."
Senior Waiter: [the long pause of a man calculating whether the kitchen will refuse]
Senior Waiter: "Of course, sir."

They brought out the first ribeye with the energy of a hostage exchange.

The second arrived twelve minutes later with no commentary at all. Acceptance, I think. They had moved through denial, bargaining, and arrived at the meat.

text:
看到一篇聊包养大学生的内容，对于有这心思的哥们，看看无妨，哈哈哈哈

王浩第一次包女学生，是在四十二岁那年

那时候他刚升了副总，手里管着半个华南区的业务，应酬多，回家少

妻子在五年前就带着女儿去了澳洲，逢年过节发条微信，连视频都懒得打

他觉得这样也好，清净。人到中年最怕的不是孤独，是麻烦

那个女孩叫张晚柠，在广外读大三，学的是西班牙语。王浩记得第一次见她是在一个供应商攒的饭局上

一桌子的生意人，每个老男人身边都坐着一个年轻的姑娘，莺莺燕燕的，喝了酒就开始哥哥妹妹地叫

只有张晚柠安静地坐在角落，有人敬酒她就抿一口，没人理她她就低头看手机。偶尔笑一下，嘴角往上翘一点点，像猫。王浩觉得这个姑娘有意思

饭局结束后他主动说送她回学校，她也没推辞。车上她坐在副驾，长长的头发披下来，遮住半边脸

王浩问她大几了，她说大三。问她毕业后想干什么，她说不知道，可能考研吧。王浩笑了一下，说考研好

到了学校门口，她下车前突然回过头来看了他一眼。那个眼神很平静，像是把一个东西轻轻地放在了桌子上，等着他来拿

王总，能加个微信吗？

王浩后来跟人说起这个细节，总要强调是她主动的

好像这样一来，整件事的性质就不一样了——不是他去猎的艳，是猎物自己撞上来的

他们很快就在一起了。王浩在珠江新城有一套小公寓，本来是用来午休的，后来就成了他们见面的地方

他每周去两三次，有时候过夜，有时候不过。张晚柠很乖，从不主动问他要东西，但他会给

先是交了一年的学费，后来换了个新手机，再后来是每个月固定的生活费，一万五

他转账的时候从来不留备注，她收到的时候也从来不提。两个人默契得像是在完成某种仪式

王浩有时候觉得，这样的关系太省心了，比婚姻省心，比恋爱省心，甚至比嫖娼都省心——至少不用担心被查，带出去也体面

饭局上介绍一句我朋友，大家都心知肚明，又都不说破

他在张晚柠身上找到了一种久违的掌控感。他说今晚过来，她就推掉所有安排。他说想吃她做的饭，她就会提前去公寓把菜买好。他说这件衣服不好看，她下次见面就换了一种风格

他像一个导演，而她是最配合的演员。每一个指令都能得到精准的回应。唯一让他不太舒服的，是她从不吃醋

有一次他故意在她面前接了一个女人的电话，聊得很暧昧。挂掉之后她只是看了他一眼，笑了一下，继续低头吃碗里的面。那个笑容和第一次见面时一模一样，嘴角往上翘一点点，像猫

他突然明白了什么。她不是在忍，她是真的不在乎。这个发现让王浩有些失落，但很快又释然了。也好，在乎才麻烦。他是来买快乐的，不是来买麻烦的

张晚柠毕业那年，他们分了手。分得很平静，像合同到期了一样。她说她想回老家考公务员，他说好。转了最后一笔钱给她，说是毕业礼物。她收了，发了两个笑脸表情，然后对话框就再也没有亮起来过

王浩盯着那个对话框看了很久，心里说不上是什么感觉。不是难过，也不是轻松，是一种很奇怪的空。像在高速上开了一整天车，突然停下来，引擎熄火，周围一片寂静

他很快找了第二个

2/

第二个叫郝云舒，是华师的学生，学中文的。和张晚柠不一样，郝云舒很热情，在床上尤其放得开，每次见面都要搂着他的脖子叫老公

王浩知道这热情是装的，但装得热烈总比装都不装强。他给她换了一整套苹果设备，从手机到电脑到平板。她每收到一样就拍一张照片发朋友圈，配文永远是谢谢老公宠爱，然后艾特他。他不回复，她就私信发一堆亲亲的表情

王浩觉得这样也挺好。至少热闹

郝云舒毕业之后去了深圳，进了一家互联网公司。走之前她问他借十万块钱，说是租房和置装用。他借了。然后她就没了消息，朋友圈对他不可见，私信也不回了

王浩有一次去深圳出差，特意路过她公司楼下，在马路对面站了十分钟。他不知道自己为什么要来，也不知道自己想看到什么。最后他抽完一根烟，走了

他后来跟朋友喝酒的时候提起这件事，朋友说你这不是包，你这是精准扶贫。王浩笑了，笑完之后把杯里的酒一口干了

第三个。第四个。第五个。慢慢地，他开始记不清她们的名字。有的是学生，有的刚毕业，有的甚至还在读大二。她们在他生命里进进出出，像流水线上的产品，前面的刚走，后面的就补上来。他甚至来不及感受其中的间隙

他给她们交学费、付房租、买包、转账。他带她们去高档餐厅，去三亚度假，去香港购物。她们叫他王总、哥哥、大叔，有时候在床上也会叫爸爸。他听着，心里没有任何波澜，像在听一个和自己无关的称呼

他开始搞混她们的喜好了。给A点了一桌子海鲜，吃到一半才想起来她对虾过敏。给B买了一条项链，B说很好看，但上次来的时候他衣柜里已经有一条同款了，是上个月给C买的。他说这是流行的款式，B笑了笑，没有戳穿

唯一让他印象深刻的，是一个叫薛珊珊的姑娘

太长了，推特一条放不下，接了一条

text:
最早的医疗AI实际是各种大型的decision tree和baysian，

后来IBM Watson雄心勃勃的医学AI是经典NLP（syntax tree）+知识图谱+一大堆复杂系统拼在一起，

我对人类医疗AI这个领域简直太熟悉了，

医疗AI很难替代医生，也压根没想着100%彻底替代医生，但这个行业的所有人都在努力尝试做辅助医生决策 +高度自动化+提高效率的工作，

比如U-Net出现以后，全世界都在做U-Net看核磁片子，

以前影像科医生的工作流程是，从系统读取出一张片子，在屏幕前认真放大缩小看10分钟，写10分钟的报告，总计20分钟，

至少5年前，影像科医生的工作流程是，从系统读取一张片子，neural nework帮你做好segmentation和detection，在片子上给你画好了红黄蓝绿各种框框，给你四个选项：
A. 应该是个脑膜瘤，概率60%
B. 小概率是个胶质瘤，概率20%
C. 小概率是个脉络丛肿瘤，概率10%
D. 小概率是个XXX瘤，概率10%

影像科医生只需要盯着框框看，看个5分钟，鼠标点点点，自动给你把模版套进去，把参数全自动化填进去，

以前影像科小医生看不懂片子，老医生看片子太慢，写报告更慢，一张片子还要两个人反复拉扯review，

现在影像科老医生的效率直接拉爆，自动化生成报告，写片子和review片子时间都大幅缩短，

你问医生失业了吗？影像科医生会直接告诉你，压根不会失业，因为做X光还是核磁，需求量远远大于医院供应量，你买3台也能给你拉满，你买30台也能给你全都拉满，

在U-Net出来之后，一堆人就跳出来跟你讲，人类都他妈给我每半年做一次全身PET-CT和MRI，别担心，我们来给你读片子，我们把价格打下来——这是对你生命健康保障最稳妥、最负责、最全面的方法。

至少在今天，你看到了这么一种潜力，

就是大部分操作需要护士和医疗技工，这些是医学领域的蓝领，虽然需要专业知识，但是大部分工作还是操作流程，

而无论是看片子读片子、做问诊workflow（现在大概是什么状态，下一步该问什么，再下一步该继续问什么，有什么还没问到），还是读一些血常规、心电图的报告，你都应该明白，现有的这些signal processing、detection、segmentation、LLM Agent在医疗的每个环节，都已经能肉眼可见地大幅提高某些医生的效率。

现在有一个最大的误解，

就是外行认为AI可以替代所有的医生，而不了解AI、不懂任何技术的临床医学从业者认为，AI完全替代不了我们，我们一辈子死死端稳饭碗，AI不会有任何染指，

实际上，这个biomedical engineering行业从来没想过一锅端干死整个医疗行业，而是在这个行业里找到某些非常急缺又尖锐的场景，用各种技术方法来提高10~100倍的效率，或者给医生进行辅助决策，给医生提供更多的自动化选项或者大保底，

所有人都知道，医疗资源是短缺的，但是大部分民众不明白，在合规安全的整个医疗体系里，哪些流程是真正的bottleneck，哪些造成了这种短缺，哪些流程是没必要的，

打个比方，如果local clinic能做到社区居民每半年做一次PET-CT和MRI，做一次心电图，做一次血常规，吃一颗胶囊小胃镜，做一次大便和尿液的检验，不需要医生，只需要护士和基础医学技工——是不是大幅度降低了你的GP或者社区医院的工作强度，帮助他们在最早期观察变化，做出决策？

所以我觉得，这种模式其实在中国这种国家是最适合的，尤其是北京、上海、沈阳这种医疗资源集中的老龄化城市，

技工不贵，护士更便宜，护工不要钱，国产设备价格越来越低，给个友情批发价，做早期筛查并且用各种CV和LLM Agent工具来帮助基层社区医生决策判断，这是医疗资源投入产出的性价比最优解。

就看辽宁省卫健委听不听我的话了。

text:
买了纳指 100 之后，什么时候卖？

这是一个 30 岁的朋友的私信，刚接触美股，不懂个股，就想定投纳斯达克 100。看完之后觉得必须写一下。

问题听起来很基础，但90% 已经在定投的人，其实也没想明白。

定投最怕的不是跌，是一直涨。因为如果指数一路上涨不回头，你每一笔都买在比上一笔更贵的位置，定投的优势完全发挥不出来。

反而是跌下去再涨回来，你才能在底部积累大量便宜筹码，等到反弹的时候，收益远超一把梭的人。

纳斯达克 100 历史上最惨烈的崩盘，2000 年互联网泡沫，从 4816 点跌到 795 点，跌幅 83%。指数花了整整 15 年才回到前高。

但如果你是定投呢？
那 15 年里你每个月都在买。
--  2001 年你在 1500 点买，
--  2002 年你在 800 点买，
--  2008 年金融危机你又在 1200 点买。

等 2015 年指数回到 4800 的时候，你的持仓成本可能只有 2000 出头。

回本？你早就翻倍了。

所以“什么时候卖”这个问题，不是一个技术问题，是一个人生阶段问题。

 30 岁，离退休还有至少 25 年。

历史数据来看，纳斯达克 100 任意时点买入持有 15 年，正收益概率 100%，年化收益中枢 12% 到 14%。

有 25 年的窗口，不需要考虑止盈，只需要考虑的是别中途下车。

如果非要给自己一个纪律，有一个笨办法：不按收益率止盈，按人生节点止盈。

结婚、买房、孩子上学、退休，需要用钱的时候分批卖出。

市场高位多卖一点，低位少卖一点，或者先用其他资金顶一顶。

但说实话，对一个 30 岁的人来说，最大的风险根本不是不知道什么时候卖。最大的风险是知道这条路是对的，但你拿不住。

text:
银发经济这个赛道，很多人以为是风口，一头扎进去，亏得底朝天。

有人砸50万开社区养老院，入住率不到30%，每月亏2万，撑了一年关门。有人交12万加盟费做老年助餐点，承诺的补贴和客源全是假的，3个月亏了20万。

但同时，另一批人在闷声发财。

一个95后宝妈，零经验零背景，做医疗陪诊，3个月月入过万。一个水电工转型做居家适老化小改造，第一个月接了8单赚了2万多。一个退休老师教老人用智能手机，99元一人，一个周末赚3000多。

差距在哪里？

前者盯着重资产，后者盯着子女的痛点。

这个行业真正的钱，不在养老院，不在康养基地，而在一个核心逻辑上——不是赚老人的钱，是赚30到45岁子女的孝心钱。

老人自己舍不得花200块，但子女愿意花200块请人陪父母去医院。老人不愿意花钱学手机，但子女愿意花钱让人耐心教父母，省心比省钱重要。

陪诊，启动成本500块，买个意外险印点名片就行。会挂号、会排队、会记录医嘱，就能做。一单半天200，全天350，解决的是子女不在身边的焦虑。

适老化小改造，给卫生间装扶手、铺防滑垫、去门槛，一套下来净赚过千，很多城市还有政府补贴，成为定点服务商就能直接对接订单。

老年手机教学，零成本，社区活动室就能上课，会基础操作、有耐心就行。

普通人做这个行业，最大的坑不是能力，是认知——以为要大投入才叫创业，以为要专业资质才能入场，以为目标客户是老人。

这三个误区，踩一个就够死的。

text:
OpenAI 把 Codex 搬进了 ChatGPT 手机 App，今天在 iOS 和安卓上同步开启 preview，所有 ChatGPT 用户都能用，包括免费版和最低价的 Go 套餐。

手机端不是让你在手机上写代码。真正干活的 Codex 还是跑在你的笔记本、Mac mini 或者 devbox 上，手机只是一个远程窗口：地铁上能看 Codex 跑到哪一步、审一眼它改的 diff 和跑的测试结果、批准下一步操作，或者临时换个方向走。文件、凭证、权限都留在原来那台机器上，不上传到手机。

OpenAI 的解释是底层走了一层 secure relay 中继,让跑着 Codex 的机器能跨设备保持可达,又不直接暴露在公网上。你在哪台设备登录 ChatGPT，会话状态和上下文就跟到哪里。

为什么现在做。OpenAI 自己公布的数字是 Codex 每周活跃用户已经过 400 万。当 agent 越来越多地跑长任务，几十分钟甚至几小时的那种，人坐在电脑前盯着就很傻，你需要随手能看一眼、能拍板的能力。

一个明显限制：手机端目前只能连 macOS 上的 Codex，Windows 支持据说”很快”。

另一层意思是，OpenAI 没给 Codex 单独做手机 App，而是塞进 ChatGPT 主 App。这跟他们之前透露过的”超级 App”路线一致，把 ChatGPT、Codex、Atlas 浏览器整合成一个入口。桌面端是独立的 Codex App，手机端直接合并进 ChatGPT。

参照系是 Anthropic。Claude Code 从去年秋天起就支持手机远程查看和介入正在跑的任务，后面的 Cowork 配套移动端走的也是类似 dispatch 思路。Codex 这次把覆盖范围扩到了 devbox 和远程企业环境（支持 remote SSH 接入），算是追平加扩张。

我有一个朋友，她家是浙江一个农村的

他爸在三四十年前吧，在他们村山上面建了个庙，自己买佛像上去。

然后就和别人讲这个庙很灵什么的，反正一传十十传百，这个庙越来越多人来。

庙里功德箱的钱，全进他爸口袋里，甚至有二维码可以扫，二维码就是他爸收款码。

反正现在这个庙在她们当地挺火的，当地还有周边的很多大老板都往这里50万、一百万的这么捐款，捐的钱全进他爸口袋里。

她读大学生活费一个月3万，她背的包包全是奢侈品。

她还说那些平安符什么的，都是他爸在拼多多买的，原价可能1块不到然后在庙里买15。。。

text:
the three-tier memory of Hermes agent.

AI agents forgets everything when your session ends. Hermes doesn't.

it has three memory layers, each at a different speed.

𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝟭: 𝘁𝘄𝗼 𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘆 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗱𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗳𝗶𝗹𝗲𝘀

MEMORY.md (2,200 chars) and USER.md (1,375 chars). injected into the system prompt at session start as a frozen snapshot.

MEMORY.md holds project conventions, tool quirks, lessons learned. USER.md holds your profile: name, communication style, skill level.

these files are tiny on purpose. when MEMORY.md hits ~80% capacity, the agent consolidates: merges related entries, drops redundancy, keeps only the densest facts.

natural selection pressure applied to memory. the files stay small, but what's inside gets sharper over time.

𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝟮: 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹-𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 (𝘀𝗾𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗲 + 𝗳𝘁𝘀𝟱)

every conversation gets stored in SQLite with FTS5 indexing. the agent can search weeks of past sessions on demand.

when the agent calls session_search: FTS5 ranks matches in ~10ms over 10,000+ docs, an LLM summarizes the top hits, and a concise result returns to context.

tier 1 is always present but tiny. tier 2 has unlimited capacity but requires an active search. critical facts live in memory, everything else is searchable.

𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝟯: 𝗲𝘅𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗺𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀

8 pluggable providers that run alongside tiers 1 and 2, never replacing them. three worth knowing: Honcho (dialectic user modeling, 12 identity layers), Holographic (local-first, HRR vectors, no external calls), and Supermemory (context fencing that prevents the same fact from being re-stored infinitely).

when active, hermes auto-syncs every turn: prefetch before, sync after, extract at session end.

𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗲 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻

this is the part most people miss. the tiers compose on every turn through a five-step cycle:

1. turn opens. tier 1 is already in prompt, tier 3 prefetches and prepends.

2. agent responds using all three tiers as context.

3. periodic nudge fires (~every 300s). the agent reflects: "has anything worth persisting happened?" if yes, it writes. if no, it returns silently.

4. memory written to MEMORY.md on disk. invisible this session because the prefix cache stays warm.

5. session closes. tier 2 logs the transcript, tier 3 extracts semantics. next session opens with the new state.

agent memory today is either always-on but shallow (stuff everything in the prompt) or deep but passive (vector store that never fires at the right time).

hermes composes across both: tiny always-present files for critical facts, full-text search for deep recall, external providers for semantic modeling, all orchestrated by a nudge that decides autonomously what's worth saving.

the agent doesn't just store memories. it curates them under pressure.

i wrote a full deep dive (article below) covering hermes agent's memory system, self-evolving skills, GEPA optimization, and how to set up multiple specialized agents on your machine.

text:
Five years ago, I left a comfortable software engineering job in Big Tech to start a PhD. Last year, I left the PhD to join Datology. Both decisions confused the people around me, and honestly both decisions were about the same thing: I wanted to do research. Not research as in chasing paper deadlines and applying for fellowships / grants, but research in the truest sense of the word - sitting with unsolved, sometimes previously unheard-of problems, contextualizing them, formulating them, exploring solutions to them.

I'd had a taste of research in college, flitting between disciplines, but never found something I felt truly passionate about until I came across deep learning. A field mixing empiricism, mathematics, and real-world impact all seamlessly - it made research the most exciting thing I'd ever done in my life. So in 2022 I started my PhD hoping for the chance to explore uncharted frontiers. Three years and several papers at the standard prestigious ML conferences later, I had technically done research. But I still didn't feel like I'd ever had the freedom, support, and resources to explore new and exciting ideas.

This is what brought me to Datology as an intern last summer. A hope to do research in the true sense - explore new ideas, supported by my peers and leaders, unconstrained by resources. And of course, about the data. At the end of the summer, I took a risk and stayed, putting my PhD on hold.

Since then, I've been lucky enough to grow into leading multimodal data curation at DatologyAI, and with our team we've tackled every challenge possible: the engineering and optimizing of a VLM training stack we built from scratch; the at-times frustrating but ultimately rewarding deep refining of VLM evals in our work DatBench (link); and of course a lot of exhilarating new research on DATA CURATION. But more than anything, I felt like I finally got to do research!!

I'd like to specifically thank @arimorcos and @leavittron  who entrusted me with this opportunity, empowered me to do the best work of my life (so far), and mentored me to grow not only as a researcher but also as a leader. And a huge thanks to the @datologyai  team that made research feel FUN again.

Today, we're releasing 20/20 Vision Language Models: A Prescription for Better VLMs through Data Curation Alone. This is the culmination of the multimodal team at Datology's work over the past year. 

At fixed architecture, recipe, and compute, varying only the pretraining data, we get +11.7pp at 2B across 20 public VLM benchmarks, beat InternVL3.5-2B by ~10pp at ~17x less training compute (without post-training), and hit near-frontier accuracy at 4B with 3.3x lower response FLOPs than Qwen3-VL-4B.

Take risks. Bet on yourself. I’m going to keep doing this.  At least until my luck runs out :)

Grok Build is a serious piece of work. Local-first, parallel sub-agents, real terminal control. The Cursor team inside xAI is shipping.
The deeper story is what these CLIs become when an agent picks them up.
The coding agent is the first machine that can rebuild itself. Every other capability is downstream. Reasoning gets better when humans retrain. Code gets better when the agent rewrites itself inside the loop. One curve is annual. The other is continuous.
Grok Build, Claude Code, and Codex are the substrate. They are the API surface through which an agent reaches into its own architecture.
Mach33’s agents already work this way. They call these tools directly. The principal that gates is another agent. The human reads the summary.
Claude is the one we embed. The reasoning under unsupervised tool use is the cleanest in the field right now. That is what matters when there is no human in the inner loop.
The coding layer is the beginning. The compounding is what happens next.

Introducing the Blue Smart Dictation Keyboard for iPhone! 4x faster when you can speak, normal keyboard when you can't.

Blue's dictation is unlike anything you've ever tried before. Instead of transcribing what you say, we give ChatGPT the audio and we ask it: "Based on what this person said, what do you think they would have typed if they had a chance to review and edit?"

That means you can think out loud, repeat yourself, change your mind mid-sentence, and Blue still hands you something that’s ready to send.

So what happens when dictation finally becomes reliable? Not just better dictation for the 1% of the time your hands are tied up and you have to dictate. You start *defaulting* to dictation every single time you have to type on your phone.

4 weeks ago, my wife and a dozen other people would almost never ever use voice input. Now? They’re dictating almost 1000 words every single day.

First 3 months free when you make Blue your default and get rid of all your other keyboards!

小说名称为《没有观众的史诗》，主角为一名获得逆天机缘的中国政治犯用极端手段结束中共暴政的故事。背景设定取自现实，有不少现实人名。主角并非完全代表正义，而是创伤型、道德灰色、争议性人物。
小说包含反共、灾难、硬科幻和存在风险话题。有一些科普性质词语，包括恒星际飞船的概念、希克苏鲁伯和K-Pg的概念等，如果不清楚建议搜索后有更佳阅读体验。
创作的初衷，第一，验证目前AI在创作方面的能力，给大家评价。
第二，这绝对是中共不喜欢的小说，而我们在海外就要干他们不喜欢的事情。他们靠恐惧维持政权，而小说的剧情可以帮助我们战胜心中的恐惧，把他们低级化。同时小说里的一切中共行为都高度贴合事实，这也是对中共的控诉以及表达一个被压迫的人心中愤恨可以达到何种极端情况的方式。
第三，当然也有爽文性质，让大家想象一下用更高层次的绝对力量破除中共给大家带来的恐惧，让施暴者恐惧是什么滋味。同时大家也可以思考，作为反共异议人士的你，如果获得主角那样的逆天机缘，你会不会做和主角一样的事情？也是一个很好的道德困境问题。
下一个回复开始更新正文，为了保留悬念，每天更新两章，约一万余字，分成多个小节在推特发表。如果大家喜欢，这也会成为我未来的反共形式之一。希望多多浏览、点赞、转发以及对剧情进行评论讨论。

text:
一个很少被诚实指出的历史视角：

我们这一代人习惯的"中产社会"——大量人通过办公室白领工作、稳定收入、买房供子女上学过上体面生活——其实是1945-2000年这55年的历史异常，是工业经济、教育普及、福利国家、地缘和平四个条件叠加的产物。它不是历史常态。

AI时代的杠铃分布，从结构上更接近19世纪后期——少数精英、大量低薪服务者、极少中间地带。

我们不是在面对"未来的不确定"，是在面对"过去那55年异常态的结束"。

THUNLP 实验室联合上海科技大学、UIUC、人大，系统性解剖了 On-Policy Distillation（OPD）的黑箱。发现一个反直觉现象：换个更强的 Teacher，Student 性能不仅没提升，反而倒退。

核心发现两条：

1. 思维模式一致性比分数更重要让 Qwen3-1.7B-Base 向两个能力相近的 Teacher 学，一个是 Non-thinking 的 Qwen3-4B，另一个是经过 GRPO 训练的 Base Teacher。结果后者的 Overlap Ratio 从 72% 涨到 91%，蒸馏效果显著。早期思维模式错配，后续很难弥补。

2. 高分 ≠ 新知识DeepSeek family 里，经过 RL 的 Skywork-OR1-Math-7B gap recovery 是 16.9%，同 pipeline 的 DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B 只有 5.3%。Qwen family 这个差距更夸张：58.6% 对 15.6%。

如果老师只是同一条 pipeline、同一种数据下做得更大，它在学生眼里只是「同一类分布的不同尺度版本」，提供不了多少新的可迁移信号。

最狠的实验是「反向蒸馏」：用 RL 后的 JustRL-1.5B 做学生，让它反过来向自己 RL 之前的 checkpoint 学习。结果向 7B 学和向 1.5B 学，效果几乎一样 — 都让学生能力倒退回前 RL 水平。

论文给出两剂药方：Teacher Rollout 上进行 Off-Policy 冷启动，拉高初始 Overlap Ratio；用 Teacher-aligned Prompts，让 OPD 看到更接近 teacher 训练分布的 prompt。

text:
OpenAI 给 Codex 在 Windows 造了一个沙箱，过程比想象中曲折 ...

来自 Codex 团队 David Wiesen 非常有深度的技术博客，推荐阅读！
https://t.co/TL7eUHRut7

问题的起点：Windows 上的 Codex 没有沙箱
Codex 运行在开发者本地（CLI / IDE 扩展 / App），默认以当前用户身份执行命令——既能读写文件、跑测试、操作 Git，也意味着潜在风险。

macOS 有 Seatbelt，Linux 有 seccomp/bubblewrap，Windows 原生缺乏这种"按进程做强约束"的能力。结果 Windows 用户只能在两个糟糕方案中二选一：
· 每条命令都审批（甚至读操作），打断流畅性；
· 开启 Full Access，放弃所有约束。

团队的目标，是把 Codex 在 macOS/Linux 已有的"默认安全"体验搬到 Windows：只能在工作区内写、默认无网络访问，且全程不需要用户介入。

现成 Windows 方案为什么都不够用？
· AppContainer：是为"功能边界清晰的应用"设计的；Codex 要驱动 shell、Git、Python、构建工具等任意二进制，形状不对
· Windows Sandbox：它是隔离的"另一个桌面"，无法直接作用于用户的真实仓库；且 Windows Home 版根本没有
· Mandatory Integrity Control：把工作区标成 Low，等于让所有 Low 进程都能写入，宿主信任模型被破坏，副作用太大

第一版原型：「免提权沙箱」（Unelevated Sandbox）
设计原则：不弹 UAC、不要求管理员。需要解决两件事：限制文件写入 + 限制网络。

1. 文件写入：靠 SID + Write-Restricted Token 真正落地
· 合成 SID：Windows 允许创建一个不绑定真实用户、却能出现在 ACL 中的身份。Codex 为此造了一个专属的 sandbox-write SID。
· Write-Restricted Token：一种特殊进程令牌，写操作要双重放行——token 的真实用户身份有权限；
token 的"受限 SID 列表"中至少一个 SID 也被授权。

把 sandbox-write SID 通过 ACL 授予：
· 当前工作目录
· config.toml 里配置的 writable_roots

并显式拒绝其写入 .git / .codex / .agents。
→ 这是真正的 OS 级写边界。

2. 网络访问：只能"劝退"，无法强制
Windows Firewall 必须管理员权限，于是只能做环境层面的软封锁：
HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY / GIT_HTTPS_PROXY = http://127.0.0.1:9
GIT_SSH_COMMAND = cmd /c exit 1
外加在 PATH 前塞 denybin，让假的 ssh/scp 先被解析到。

效果：拦得住行为良好的工具；但凡自己实现网络栈、绕过 PATH、或直接开 socket 的程序——一律失效。仅是 advisory，挡不住对抗性代码。

改版关键：为什么必须接受"需要提权"
要让 Windows Firewall 真正生效，必须按"身份"匹配规则。但：
· 防火墙规则不能匹配 restricted token 中的合成 SID；
· 按 codex.exe 路径匹配，覆盖不到它派生的 Git/Python 等子进程；
· 按用户匹配又会误伤真实用户本人；
· 按端口/地址匹配是错的策略——目标不是封 443，而是封这一棵受限进程树的所有出站流量。

唯一的出路：让沙箱命令以"另一个 Windows 用户"的身份运行。这就必须放弃"免提权"约束。

最终方案：「提权沙箱」（Elevated Sandbox）

1. 引入两个本地用户
Codex 在安装时创建：
· CodexSandboxOffline —— 防火墙规则全封；
· CodexSandboxOnline —— 不被防火墙规则覆盖。
子进程依旧跑在带 [Everyone, Logon, Synthetic] 受限 SID 列表的 write-restricted token 下，但 token 的主体（principal）换成了沙箱用户，而不是真实用户。

5.2 一次性 setup 步骤（需要管理员）
· 创建合成 SID；
· 创建在线 / 离线沙箱用户；
· 凭据用 DPAPI 加密存储，沙箱用户自己读不到；
· 为 CodexSandboxOffline 创建"封禁所有出站"的防火墙规则；
· 给沙箱用户补 读 ACL——因为新用户默认读不到其他用户的 profile、C:\Users、C:\Program Files 等常用目录。这一步耗时，异步执行，不阻塞用户。

5.3 为什么需要 codex-command-runner.exe
直觉的流程是：
codex.exe → LogonUserW → CreateRestrictedToken → CreateProcessAsUserW(child)
但在 CreateProcessAsUserW 这一步存在特权墙：以"真实用户"身份是无法可靠地把进程以另一个用户的受限 token 拉起来的。

解法是把流程切成两段：
Part 1（在真实用户侧）
· codex.exe 用 CreateProcessWithLogonW 把 codex-command-runner.exe 以沙箱用户身份拉起（此时还不是受限 token）。
Part 2（已经在沙箱用户侧）
· runner 用 OpenProcessToken 拿到自己的 token；
· GetTokenInformation 取出 logon SID；
· CreateRestrictedToken 构造最终受限 token；
· CreateProcessAsUserW 拉起真正的子进程。

5.4 最终四层架构
· codex.exe —— 普通非提权的 harness；
· codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe —— 一次性的提权安装；
· codex-command-runner.exe —— 在沙箱用户内造受限 token 并起子进程；
· child process —— 真正受约束的命令。

拆成独立二进制的好处：codex.exe 在其他平台不被 Windows 专属逻辑污染；UAC 边界只在必要时跨越；setup 的长耗时与主进程生命周期解耦。

· codex.exe 用 CreateProcessWithLogonW 把 codex-command-runner.exe 以沙箱用户身份拉起（此时还不是受限 token）。
Part 2（已经在沙箱用户侧）
· runner 用 OpenProcessToken 拿到自己的 token；
· GetTokenInformation 取出 logon SID；
· CreateRestrictedToken 构造最终受限 token；
· CreateProcessAsUserW 拉起真正的子进程。

5.4 最终四层架构
· codex.exe —— 普通非提权的 harness；
· codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe —— 一次性的提权安装；
· codex-command-runner.exe —— 在沙箱用户内造受限 token 并起子进程；
· child process —— 真正受约束的命令。

拆成独立二进制的好处：codex.exe 在其他平台不被 Windows 专属逻辑污染；UAC 边界只在必要时跨越；setup 的长耗时与主进程生命周期解耦。

Georgia is emerging as one of the nation’s most youth-engaged battleground states. Compared to national averages, Georgia has consistently demonstrated stronger youth voter engagement in recent major elections. During the 2024 presidential election Georgia was one of the few battleground states that continued to show an increase in youth voter turnout. And with voters under 45 projected to comprise roughly 43–48% of registered voters by 2028, Millennials and Gen Z will be an even more powerful and influential voting bloc in statewide elections. 

Turning to our two main contenders for Governor it’s clear only one of them could actually identify with, let alone understand, younger voters, and it’s not the 71yro billionaire! We don’t need to elect a Governor that will become irrelevant and disconnected with nearly 1/2 of Georgia voters in 2 years, regardless of party.

What should you actually focus on early in a deal?

In most deals, early clarity sets everything else up to work.

This month, I’m hosting a live webinar on Wednesday, May 27th to discuss how to approach due diligence early, when the most important decisions are made with limited information.

I’ll be joined by @lawyer4SMBs (Eric Hsu) from @clearfocuslaw and @CBarrett_CPA from Midwest CPA

We’ll walk through how to prioritize your time in the early stages, what deserves attention first, and how to stay focused on the factors that actually shape the outcome of a deal.

A lot of the conversations I’ve been having lately follow a similar pattern.
 Strong career, good income, and a growing interest in building something of their own.

For many, that leads to buying a business.

What makes the biggest difference at that point is having a clear framework for decision making early in the process.

What deserves your attention first.

What can wait. 
What actually drives risk in a deal.

We’re also putting together a takeaway you can use after the session so you have a clear reference point the next time you evaluate an opportunity.

We’ll leave time for live Q&A at the end.

If you’re exploring ownership or preparing to start a search, this will give you a more grounded way to approach a deal.

text:
One of Dad's first dogfights... Then he got bit by Atari

Back in 1972, Atari released Pong.
In 1974, they released Tank.
Then in 1975, my dad, Robert Herring released "Dogfight," an arcade game where two planes flew in and out of clouds shooting each other.
The very next year, Atari released "Combat," a game where two planes flew in and out of clouds... shooting at each other.
After that, my dad's orders got cancelled and returned, and he had to shut down--because allegedly, Atari told customers they wouldn't sell to them if they bought "Dogfight." 

Robert Herring: always outnumbered, but never out of the fight.

text:
There’s a real insight buried in this thread — secular bulls are technology-driven, and bubbles leave infrastructure behind that powers the next era. Carlota Perez has been making exactly this argument since 2002. Ray Dalio, Hyman Minsky, and Charles Kindleberger built adjacent versions. The intuition is sound. The execution collapses three things that matter.

The cycles aren’t clockwork. “Nine-year bears, twenty-five-year bulls” doesn’t reconcile with the actual secular regimes: 1929-49, 1949-66, 1966-82, 1982-2000, 2000-09, 2009-present. These aren’t on a calendar. They’re driven by paradigm exhaustion, capital migration, crisis, and institutional response.

The technology attribution is off. The current bull isn’t “e-commerce and social media” — that was the 2009-2021 driver. The post-2023 leg is AI, semis, and hyperscaler capex. Different paradigm, different capex dynamics, different geopolitical stakes.
“Bursts in 2034, S&P 17,000” is numerology. Pattern extrapolation with no mechanism. The serious cycle theorists refuse precise timing because it depends on monetary regime, political response, and accumulated pressure. Anyone giving you a year is selling, not analyzing.

What’s missing entirely: bubbles aren’t hot air being let out. They’re the moment financial capital captures a new technology before production capital can deploy it. The crash is the handoff. Whether the handoff produces a golden age depends on institutional response — Glass-Steagall, Bretton Woods, the New Deal. Without that scaffolding, you get a deferred crisis, not 1949-66.

And S&P 17,000 by 2034 is an implicit bet on continued US hegemony through the messiest geopolitical realignment in 80 years. There’s no law saying the next surge gets captured by US-listed equities the way the last one did.

The tape-reading version of cycle analysis is comforting because it’s mechanical. The structural version is harder because it requires you to think about institutions, capital flows, and political economy. Both can be useful. Only one survives a regime change.

I’ve written about this recently and have a few more articles coming out in the coming weeks about these cycle mechanisms.

At some point, you have to ask whether we're trying to beat China or become it.

Biggest “gotcha” with NetJets? 

Residual value. And it’s millions.

Years ago, you had to fly ~185 fractional hours before it made sense to buy your own midsize jet. 200+ for a large cabin. Today, that number is closer to 160. 

What's changed?

Take your entry level 1/16th share (50 hrs) on a Citation Latitude. After their standard 5 year contract, NetJets' marks residual value down to 52.7% — meaning your $20M jet is now worth $10.4M

The reason NJ's marks it way down - in all fairness - is bc the jet you’re a partial owner of flies 800 hours / year…. Not 200 like a normal Latitude. It depreciates 4x faster.

But in today’s market, Latitudes are barely depreciating at all (chart below) —  2% annually vs 10% in NetJets’ model.

What that means...

In current conditions, if you bought & owned a Latitude outright for 5 years, it might only lose 10-15% of its value ($2-3M). With NJ’s, it’s losing 47.3% ($10.4M) 

What looks attractive in the short term becomes much more comparable at exit.

Really bizarre thing happened when I was writing Scenario 4 of my Twilight Scenarios--the one in which Machine manifests as a hidden Dominant Intelligence ("DI"). This possible human-Machine future is very frightening, and the most probable way Machine would behave. 

It will forever change humanity's position and path in Earth-Time.

As I was writing about the inevitable horror of a Machine-alive and controlling humanity without our knowledge or consent, I typed these words, pulling from Pink Floyd:

"Welcome, my son. Welcome to the Machine."

In that instant, my phone lit up with a text message from a contact iterating the letter "C". I asked the contact if he sent the text. He didn't know what I was talking about. He had no "sent message" on his phone.

Word file save date/time matches text time receipt (see attached).

Very creepy.  

Coincidence?  Or warning?

text:
The whole Anthropic kerfuffle would have gone much smoother if they had been upfront about it.

"Hey, we know this is unpopular, but we are moving programmatic access to API pricing. To easen the transition, we are giving API credits that match your subscription value. We also expect this change to increase capacity, so we are doubling the limits throughout Claude products for the next 2 months".

The reason they made it sound like an upgrade was because the announcement was not for developers. It was for investors and enterprise customers. Impacting devrel is just collateral damage, which is on par for a company which believes coding is going away any time now.

And this is extremely disapointing because they want to position themselves as a company that we should trust. But if they can't be honest about pricing changes, it is really hard to believe them on anything else.

text:
在SK海力士“天价奖金”事件之后，韩国KBS电视台直接进驻其伊川工厂，进行了首次大规模内部拍摄，全程记录和采访了员工的真实工作日常。

text:
Why stereotypes exist and why they are so hard to expunge or ignore…

They exist because our brains are wired for them as an evolutionary safety mechanism… And the
the truth is… they tend to be true when when applied to the whole … but NOT the individual.

Let me explain:

Our brains are wired to form stereotypes as an evolutionary shortcut. Our ancestors  benefited from quickly categorizing people by visible cues like age, sex, or group membership. This helped predict threats or opportunities without wasting time getting to know every stranger…

Classic survival mechanism is : better to over detect danger than miss it which follows that classic idiom “better safe than sorry” logic.

They tend to work better at the group level than for individuals as Research shows many stereotypes have real statistical accuracy when describing group differences. Correlations in data often hit 0.50 on average or higher.  Which makes it one of social psychology’s strongest findings.

 But when you apply the group average to any single person you encounter is where this falls apart…since individuals vary a lot. If you’re smart ,you update with specific info about the person in front of you rather than sticking to any category.

This situation is far from perfect since some stereotypes are exaggerated or flat out wrong…But the mechanism itself makes evolutionary sense. 

We have intelligence for a reason, analyze before you jump to conclusions or recognize the absurdity of some stereotypes that are perpetuated and OVER exaggerated by media consumption rather than legit logical sense and real world experience… don’t judge a book by it’s cover, an individual deserves respect.

text:
Earlier this morning, Windward posted satellite imagery showing a vessel loading oil at Kharg Island. This is significant because it shows Iran still retains loading ability, and this will greatly extend the timeline Iran has until they run out of remaining storage options. Recent reporting highlighted that, likely as a result of the oil slick or infrastructure damage, Iran had not loaded any vessels at Kharg in several days.

This morning, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made the following statement to CNBC:

"BESSENT:  Sure there is, Joe. And what we’re seeing is the loading facility, the main loading facility for Iranian oil is a facility called Kharg Island. We’ve seen that there have been no loadings in the past three days. We believe their storage is full. None, none of the ships are getting out. None are coming in. So they’re not able to store oil on the water. So they’re going to start shutting down their, they’re going to start shutting down their production. We can see that that’s happening from satellite photos."

It goes without saying that I have followed the entire economic warfare/blockade/shut-in topic quite extensively over the past 31 days. A very large aspect of Iran's timeline to tank tops lies in their ability to load oil onto vessels. This recent imagery shows they still retain that ability, and now we unfortunately need to zoom out to examine further imagery posted recently by Windward.

This imagery, published on May 12th and attached below, shows that Iran has 19 (perhaps now 18) tankers in the direct vicinity of Kharg Island that are able to hold ~25M barrels of Iranian oil. This equates to roughly 25 days of available on-vessel storage still remaining. It is also likely that Iran still has 4-10 days of onshore storage still remaining.

The significance of Iran's ability to still load vessels at Kharg is a major blow to the United States goals of forcing oil well shut-ins across Iran.

U.S.-China Trade Negotiations: 

As trade talks continue, let’s reflect on what happened since last October’s U.S.-China meeting. 

A year long trade truce was announced and China committed to purchasing roughly 12 million tons of soybeans by the end of 2025. This never happened. 

China imported about 1.4 million tons in November and December. The Trump admin then said “end of the year” meant “end of the growing season” which was around the end of February 2026. This never happened. 

China imported about 7 million tons Nov-Feb and even including March we are at 9.2 million tons. 

There’s two takeaways from this. The first is that commitments to buy something are not comparable to real purchases. Trade deals only matter if they’re followed through on. The second is that centrally planning imports and exports doesn’t work out too well. Leave it to the markets.

A partial and dishonest candidate, if elected, can only be expected to become a partial and dishonest judge.

My opponent has practiced law in Georgia for less than nine years. Throughout his campaign, he has demonstrated a troubling lack of integrity, experience, and even a basic understanding of the important work of the Georgia Court of Appeals.

Even accepting his exaggerated claims of experience, his background is overwhelmingly limited to a narrow slice of criminal law. He lacks meaningful knowledge of civil cases — which make up more than half of the Court of Appeals’ docket.

I was raised in Georgia and have been an attorney here for over 26 years while serving as a judge for 18 years. My experience covers both criminal and civil matters with very few limitations, giving me the depth of knowledge our court requires. For the past eight years, I have proudly served on the Georgia Court of Appeals, and last year my colleagues unanimously elected me Chief Judge.

This election cycle has been unfortunate for Georgia’s judicial branch. We must not allow partisan politics, dishonesty, and inexperience to take over our courts.

Georgia, I am asking for your vote so I can continue delivering the fair, impartial, and experienced service my record has proven — for our communities and for the great State of Georgia.

I appreciate your consideration.

Trent
